P:Sine substitution with a cotangent (Example 7.5)|S:Find $dx$ and $\sqrt{9-x^2}$ in terms of θ.L:dx = -3\cos\theta\,d\theta,\quad \sqrt{9-x^2} = 3\cos\thetaL:dx = 3\cos\theta\,d\theta,\quad \sqrt{9-x^2} = -3\cos\thetaL:dx = 3\cos\theta\,d\theta,\quad \sqrt{9-x^2} = 3 - 3\sin\thetaL:dx = 3\cos\theta\,d\theta,\quad \sqrt{9-x^2} = 3\cos\thetaL:dx = 3\cos\theta\,d\theta,\quad \sqrt{9-x^2} = 9\cos\thetaL:dx = \cos\theta\,d\theta,\quad \sqrt{9-x^2} = 3\cos\theta
